title: Component Lifecycle
summary: The stages a component goes through, from created to removed.
heading: Component Lifecycle

blocks.text: Every component is born, lives on the screen for a while, and is eventually removed. Angular lets you run your own code at these moments by adding special methods called lifecycle hooks.

blocks.caption: Angular calls hooks at each stage of a component's life.

layers.title: constructor
layers.detail: Runs first; use it for injecting services, not for heavy work

layers.title: ngOnInit
layers.detail: Runs once after the component is set up; good for initial loading

layers.title: ngOnChanges
layers.detail: Runs whenever an input value changes

layers.title: ngOnDestroy
layers.detail: Runs just before the component is removed; clean up here

blocks.text: To use a hook, implement its interface and add the method. Here the component loads data when it starts and cleans up when it leaves.

blocks.label: timer.ts

blocks.text: With signals and computed, you often need fewer hooks — Angular reacts to changes for you. But ngOnInit and ngOnDestroy are still very common.
Lifecycle hooks need a real component being created and destroyed, so try this one in your own Angular app — add a console.log in each hook and watch the order in the browser console.
Angular has a few more hooks for advanced cases. You'll rarely reach for these as a beginner, but here they are for completeness.

layers.title: ngOnChanges
layers.detail: Runs whenever an input value changes (before ngOnInit the first time)

layers.title: ngDoCheck
layers.detail: Runs on every change-detection pass; for your own custom change checks

layers.title: ngAfterContentInit
layers.detail: Once, after projected content (ng-content) is ready

layers.title: ngAfterContentChecked
layers.detail: After Angular checks the projected content

layers.title: ngAfterViewInit
layers.detail: Once, after the component's view and child views are ready

layers.title: ngAfterViewChecked
layers.detail: After Angular checks the component's view

blocks.text: The "Checked" hooks run very often, so keep them light. Most apps only ever need ngOnInit and ngOnDestroy.

items: Lifecycle hooks run your code at key moments.
ngOnDestroy runs before removal — clean up there.
Implement the matching interface to use a hook.
